stimulus.source_note: Photograph: Elvis Presley, 1956 publicity portrait. Public domain (published in the United States in 1956 without a copyright notice), via Wikimedia Commons.
stimulus.text: The photograph is a 1956 publicity portrait of Elvis Presley, a white singer from Memphis, Tennessee. Presley, with his slicked-back hair, became the most famous performer of the new rock 'n' roll music.

stem: Many adults in the 1950s feared rock 'n' roll most of all because of what about the music?

options.text: Its roots and many performers were Black
Its stars came from lower-class Southern families
options.misconception: Background from the books: Elvis was Southern and working-class, but that was not what most frightened adults.
Background from the books: rock lyrics were about love, cars, and dancing, not communism.

options.text: Its songs were written in foreign languages
options.misconception: Rock songs were sung in English, so language was never the issue.

rationales.A: Background from the books: rock grew out of rhythm and blues and other Black music, and its crossing of the color line frightened a segregated society.
rationales.B: Background from the books: Elvis was Southern and working-class, but that was not what most frightened adults.
rationales.C: Background from the books: rock lyrics were about love, cars, and dancing, not communism.
rationales.D: Rock songs were sung in English, so language was never the issue.
rationales.general:
1. Ask what set rock apart from the music adults already knew.
2. Background from the books: rock grew from Black music, rhythm and blues, gospel, and the blues, and Black performers reached white teenagers.
3. Background from the books: in a segregated society, music that crossed the color line looked dangerous to many adults.
Remember: Fear of a new music often points to the social line the music crosses.
